selected.title: The Florist Called About His Other Anniversary
selected.hook: A florist called me because my boyfriend's anniversary flowers had the wrong address.
selected.voiceover:
A florist called me because my boyfriend's anniversary flowers had the wrong address.

The woman asked if I could confirm the delivery for Friday. I laughed and said our anniversary was in November, not September.

She went quiet. Then she read the card: ‘Another month choosing you. Love, Daniel.’

Daniel is my boyfriend.

We've lived together for almost three years. He tells me flowers are overpriced and has bought me one bouquet our entire relationship.

I asked the florist how they even had my number. Apparently Daniel had added me as the backup contact when he created the account.

Then she mentioned it was a subscription.

Same woman. Same address. One bouquet every month for eleven months.

I didn't confront him immediately. I asked what he was doing Friday. He said overtime, probably home late.

So I asked, ‘Should I tell Maya your flowers are coming Saturday instead?’

His face changed instantly.

He admitted Maya was a coworker, but claimed the flowers were just a running joke because she'd helped him through a difficult project.

Then I showed him the card message.

He stopped calling it a joke.

He said they had feelings for each other but had never physically cheated. Apparently the monthly flowers were their way of acknowledging it without ‘crossing the line.’

I told him eleven secret anniversaries sounded like a relationship to me.

He says ending three years over flowers is ridiculous.

Would you call this cheating, even if they never touched?
selected.youtube_description:
A florist's routine delivery call exposes an anniversary that doesn't belong to the couple—and a monthly flower subscription her boyfriend never mentioned. His explanation turns a strange billing mistake into a relationship drama about emotional cheating, secret rituals, and where the line actually begins. If nothing physical happened, would the flowers still be enough for you to leave?
